description: Bullet charts are a sub-type of bar chart that is a lot easier to read.They evaluate a highlighted measure (the bullet) in comparison to a targeted measure (the target). Using a bullet chart, you can track your progress toward a goal or compare your performance to a reference line. Our IBCS-certified Bullet chart could assist you in integrating many KPI charts into one visual to present a comprehensive summary. If you have a target goal that must be met at regular intervals, a bullet chart will help you visualize your goal, the current benchmark, and the prior one in a single visual. They are best utilized for comparisons and are frequently used to compare forecasts to actual numbers. Key Feature Highlights: Chart Types – Choose between a standard bullet chart and an IBCS-certified bullet chart IBCS Bullet Chart – It's an enhanced version of the standard bullet chart which supports two types of chart templates, which are as follows: Single KPI Bullet chart – Compare any actual vs target data over a single category Multiple KPI Bullet chart - Compare multiple actuals vs target values Chart Orientation – Choose between vertical and horizontal chart orientations Comparison Band – Compare your actuals against defined value or percentage buckets. Within comparison band, we have: Comparative - assign a single value to the band field and compare it with any target/benchmark values…
